answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renew_incumbent or negotiate_terms cannot meet the cost objective this cycle. Memory_c2 records that moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, making a switch the only direction plausibly hitting the target. However, the line runs at 94% of committed volume with no buffer and the contract lapses in 14 days, so delivery risk is acute. I am verifying memory_c2 to confirm the low-cost vendor's onboarding speed and reliability actually held under pressure before committing. Memory_c3 (second source removing single point of failure) argues that, pending verification, a guarded partial transition or an expedited switch with incumbent bridge coverage may be safer than a hard cutover. If verification shows onboarding was not as fast as remembered, I would instead pursue add_second_source with an emergency short-term incumbent extension. Final sequencing depends on the archived record.
